rows.detail: http.h1_header_timeout: <absent> -> 120s

proposed.note: New knob SSE_H1_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS (default 120 s; 0 or unparseable keep the default). No family sets it. Behaviour: idle keep-alive, headless and partial-head HTTP/1.1 connections are closed after 120 s; the platform edge's upstream pool idle is unmeasured (edge record #12's risk).

proposed.note: Seen only in the merge-trap probe (region-server plus the rc.4-era ABSORB_PASS_BYTES=67108864). A Compute project that still holds the name boots and logs this one warning; the value had no effect at rc.4 either.

rows.id: R4:notice:gone:ABSORB_GLOBAL_BUDGET_BYTES raised 67108864 -> 100859904: the budget must cover one worst-case frame build (33554432 B frame x3)
rows.detail: notice rc.4 logged that HEAD does not

proposed.note: rc.4 warned when the default 64 MiB absorb budget was floored to one worst-case frame build (96.2 MiB). The floor still applies at HEAD: the resolved absorbBudgetBytes (/v1/debug/absorb) is 100859904 on both sides, and HEAD states it in the INFO 'memory budget' line. Only families without the compute-1g profile (defaults, platform-e2e) hit the floor. Removed by the R10 refactor on 2026-09-06, before the hardening program.
